subject: Urgent: Avalon spike in 5xx/429s — timeouts and retry amplification

From: Alex Roe <alex.roe@avalonrx.com>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Spike in 5xx/429s this morning — API timeouts

Hi Karthik —

We started seeing a spike in 5xx/429 responses for our Avalon MedAssist inference endpoint at ~07:50 PT this morning. Our telemetry shows a mix of 500s and intermittent 429s with high request latency (p95 > 2.4s). Customers are seeing timeouts and we have multiple automated clients retrying aggressively, which is amplifying the load.

Attached: error_manifest.csv (sample request IDs + timestamps) and request-ids-13jun.log with a few request IDs we can trace. We are on a Dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-avl-nyc-1) and this looks like capacity exhaustion + autoscaler lag — node launches are slow and queue length climbs.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood open a temporary capacity buffer for Avalon (manual attach / hot spare) so we can stabilize traffic?
- Can we fall back traffic to a compact model variant to reduce GPU memory and start serving within minutes?
- We need an ETA for mitigation steps and an exec escalation point — our CTO Susan Lee (cc'd) will be watching.

This is impacting key customers in our EHR integration pilot; please treat as high priority.

Thanks,
Alex
Principal SRE, Avalon Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Urgent: Spike in 5xx/429s this morning — API timeouts

Quick findings from a preliminary sweep of the autoscaler and runtime traces: 

Summary:
- Dedicated pool ded-avl-nyc-1 experienced sustained backlog growth starting 07:48 PT. Queue length rose from ~120 to ~980 active requests within 8 minutes.
- Node provisioning latency spiked; median node_launch_time = 210s during the spike (normal ~45s). We observed provisioning spikes correlated with a cloud provider API throttling event in the same region.
- Multiple worker processes reported OOMs when the compact LLM branch attempted larger batch sizes, leading to mid-request failure modes and 5xx responses.
- Client retry amplification: ~35% of requests in the sample log have immediate retry (no exponential backoff), which multiplied effective QPS.

Immediate mitigations enacted (08:26 PT):
1) Manual pool attach: added 4 pre-warmed nodes to dedicated-pool-avl-nyc-1 (temporary capacity). This is live now.
2) Model routing change: toggled routing rule to prefer compact variant for the Avalon route (non-disruptive soft switch, gradual cutoff).
3) Autoscaler config: switched to aggressive-provisioning profile for this tenant to reduce graceful node launch throttling while we investigate provider throttling.

Next actions (recommended):
- Keep compact variant routing for 2 hours while we monitor errors/latency.
- Postmortem with cloud provider on the region API throttling and our node_launch backoff settings.
- Recommend a dedicated reserved node pool for Avalon to avoid noisy-neighbor autoscaler dependency (billing conversations required).

Attached snapshot: autoscaler_snapshot_06-13.txt (sanitized).

I'll continue monitoring and will dump a timeline (request ids mapped to node ids) to the shared drive.

-Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
